slides.headline: He founded a university that still runs today. Decades later, India gave him its highest civilian honor - after he was gone.
Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya died on November 12, 1946, at age 84.
slides.body: A freedom fighter, educationist, and four-time president of the Indian National Congress, Malaviya is best remembered for founding Banaras Hindu University under the BHU Act of 1915 - and serving as its vice-chancellor from 1919 to 1938.

slides.headline: He stayed involved in guiding the university he built right up until his death.
slides.body: In 2014 - 68 years after his death - India posthumously awarded him the Bharat Ratna, its highest civilian honor, a day before what would have been his 153rd birth anniversary.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat is still being taught in institutions its founders built more than a century ago.
slides.body: Malaviya didn't just campaign for independence - he built an institution that has educated generations since, long after the man himself was gone.
